text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's ruling socialist party (BSP) leader Georgi Parvanov apologised to all Bulgarians who were disappointed with the BSP government. Parvanov also said he would bear his personal responsibility for BSP failure to live up to people's expectations.
-- Bulgaria's former communist leader Todor Zhivkov was freed from house arrest because of poor health. @
-- Doctors and nurses from Sofia hospitals are expected to rally in front of the Health ministry today to protest against the social policy of the ruling Socialists.

-- Bulgaria's opposition deputies were ready to stop their boycott of parliament if the ruling Socialists gave up their mandate to form a new government, Bulgaria's main opposition Union of Democratic Forces leader Ivan Kostov said. @

-- Bulgaria's oldest nuclear reactor, which was switched off last May amid international concern over its safety, was connected to the country's power grid on Monday after tests proved its metal to be safe, a Kozloduy nuclear power plant official said.
-- The executive bureau of the Socialist party decided to replace the leaders of the Socialists' parliamentary group.
-- Socialist leader Georgi Parvanov said the Socialist party needed a "clean hands"-style operation to check the incomes of all Socialist leaders since 1990.

-- Bulgaria's opposition proposed that an interim government appointed by the new president Petar Stoyanov should be given a mandate to continue talks with the Intarnational Monetary Fund on the planned introduction of a tough fixed exchange rate regime in the country. @

-- Petar Stoyanov met with leading Bulgarian economists to discuss the potential impact of planned introduction of a currency board system on the country's economy. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
